title: Diagnosis and treatment of malnutrition and sarcopenia in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HeCCMaST)
summary: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a common tumour disease with a poor prognosis. Many patients also suffer from malnutrition and muscle wasting (sarcopenia), which further worsens the course of the disease and quality of life. This study examines the nutritional status, musculature and physical performance of HCC patients during the course of their treatment. Targeted examinations are carried out to detect malnutrition and sarcopenia at an early stage. In addition, research is being conducted into the physical processes underlying these comorbidities.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of liver and intrahepatic bile ducts

interventions.name: Follow-up observation of patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) at intervals of approximately 3 months, including assessment of malnutrition and sarcopenia, BIA, muscle strength, and muscle function

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnosis of HCC based on clinical and imaging methods (sonography, NMR, CT)
Exclusion criteria:
- Pregnancy or breastfeeding
- Pacemaker or implanted defibrillator
- Insufficient ability to answer questionnaires
